description_full: China Jinmao Holdings Group Limited engages in residential and integrated property development in Mainland China. It operates through five segments: Property Development, Property Investment, Hotel Operations, Jinmao Services, and Others. The Property Development segment develops residential and comprehensive properties. The Property Investment segment leases office and retail commercial premises. The Hotel Operations segment offers hotel accommodation services, and food and beverage. The Jinmao Services segment provides property management services and community value-added services, as well as value-added services to non-property owners. The Others segment offers design and decoration services. This segment is also involved in building technology and other services. The company was formerly known as Franshion Properties (China) Limited and changed its name to China Jinmao Holdings Group Limited in September 2015. China Jinmao Holdings Group Limited was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

financial_summary: CHINA JINMAO HOLDINGS GROUP LIM is a mid-cap real estate business with a $2.0B market cap on $8.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -13% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 2% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $1M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 18.3× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 39% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
